finding: For the frozen B01 wet prescribed-qbot case, the F-AHL11 lookup candidate is consistently slower than analytical despite extremely small state error. The additional nonlinear iteration has a real end-to-end cost.
implication: The prescribed-head speed result cannot be generalized to a prescribed-flux lower boundary. Further global densification is not justified by F-AHL12C/E; a different solver-facing retention/capacity representation is required.
nonclaims: This is one prescribed-qbot case, not a complete flux-boundary matrix.
